#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# ---- workspace identity -----------------------------------------------------
worktree_root() {
  local top; top=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || die "run this inside your own git worktree of the Nxeon repo"
  top=$(readlink -f "$top")
  case "$top" in
    /opt/nxeon|/opt/nxeon-staging|/tank/nxeon-deploy/*) die "$top is a live/deploy tree. Create your own worktree first:  git -C /opt/nxeon worktree add /tank/dev-worktrees/<name> -b <branch> main" ;;
  esac
  [ -L "$top/.next" ] && die "$top/.next is a symlink (a live tree) — refusing"
  [ -L "$top/node_modules" ] && say "warning: $top/node_modules is a symlink — never 'git add -A' here (see BUILD-HOST.md). devhost does not need local node_modules at all."
  echo "$top"
}
ws_name() {
  local top="$1" n
  n=$(basename "$top" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z' | tr -c 'a-z0-9-\n' '-' | sed -E 's/-+/-/g; s/^-//; s/-$//' | cut -c1-40)
  [ -n "$n" ] || n=wt
  echo "${DEVHOST_NAME:-$n}"
}
init_ws() {
  TOP=$(worktree_root); NAME=$(ws_name "$TOP")
  case "$NAME" in *[!a-z0-9-]*|"") die "bad workspace name '$NAME' (DEVHOST_NAME=...)";; esac
  WS="$BH_ROOT/wt/$NAME"
  ENVF="/etc/nxeon-build/wt/$NAME.env"
  DBNAME="wt_$(echo "$NAME" | tr '-' '_')"
  PORT=$(( 4100 + $(printf '%s' "$NAME" | cksum | cut -d' ' -f1) % 800 ))
}

# Create the node-2 side once: dir, owner marker, throwaway DB, env file.
ensure_remote() {
  bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF >&2
set -euo pipefail
[ "\$(hostname)" = "$BUILD_HOST_NAME" ] || { echo "not node-2" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p $(q "$WS") /etc/nxeon-build/wt; chmod 700 /etc/nxeon-build/wt
mk=$(q "$WS/.devhost-owner")
if [ -f "\$mk" ] && [ "\$(cat "\$mk")" != $(q "$TOP") ]; then
  echo "workspace $NAME belongs to \$(cat "\$mk") — set DEVHOST_NAME=<unique> for $TOP" >&2; exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' $(q "$TOP") > "\$mk"
. /etc/nxeon-build/agents-db.env
if [ ! -s $(q "$ENVF") ]; then
  sec=\$(head -c 48 /dev/urandom | base64 | tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' | head -c 48)
  ( umask 077; cat > $(q "$ENVF") <<EOT
# devhost env for $NAME (node-2 only, throwaway). NEVER production values.
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://\$AGENT_PGUSER:\$AGENT_PGPASSWORD@127.0.0.1:5433/$DBNAME?connection_limit=10
AUTH_SECRET=\$sec
APP_URL=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT
PORT=$PORT
COOKIE_SECURE=false
NXEON_DEVHOST=1
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=5120
EOT
  )
fi
export PGPASSWORD="\$AGENT_PGPASSWORD"
if ! psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U "\$AGENT_PGUSER" -d postgres -tAc "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname='$DBNAME'" | grep -q 1; then
  createdb -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -U "\$AGENT_PGUSER" $DBNAME && echo "created throwaway database $DBNAME (node-2 127.0.0.1:5433)"
fi
EOF
}

push_files() {
  # Source only: git-tracked + untracked-not-ignored files. node_modules, .next,
  # .git and every .env* stay where they are (rsync never deletes excluded files).
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  rsync -a --delete --compress --compress-choice=zstd -e "ssh $BH_SSH_OPTS" \
    --exclude=/.git --exclude=/node_modules --exclude=/.next --exclude='/.next.*' \
    --exclude='/.env' --exclude='/.env.*' --include='.env.example' --exclude='.env*' \
    --exclude=/.devhost-owner --exclude=/.devhost-deps --exclude='/tsconfig.tsbuildinfo' \
    --filter=':- .gitignore' \
    "$TOP/" "$BUILD_HOST:$WS/"
}

# npm install + prisma generate when package-lock.json / schema changed (or forced).
deps() {
  local force="${1:-0}"
  bh_ssh "bash -s" <<EOF >&2
set -euo pipefail
cd $(q "$WS")
h=\$(cat package-lock.json prisma/schema.prisma 2>/dev/null | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)
if [ "$force" = 1 ] || [ ! -d node_modules ] || [ "\$(cat .devhost-deps 2>/dev/null)" != "\$h" ]; then
  echo "devhost: installing deps on node-2 (npm install + prisma generate)..."
  $(q "$BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh" agents --dir "$WS" --env "$ENVF" --unit "nxeon-dev-$NAME-deps" --max 1800 -- \
      bash -c 'npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3 && npx prisma generate 2>&1 | tail -1') </dev/null
  echo "\$h" > .devhost-deps
fi
EOF
}

prepare() { init_ws; ensure_remote; push_files; deps 0; }

REMOTE_UNIT=""
cleanup_remote_unit() {
  if [ -n "$REMOTE_UNIT" ]; then
    bh_ssh "systemctl stop $(q "$REMOTE_UNIT") 2>/dev/null; true" </dev/null || true
  fi
}

run_remote() {  # run_remote LOCK MAX CMD...
  local lock="$1" max="$2"; shift 2
  local args=(agents --dir "$WS" --env "$ENVF" --unit "nxeon-dev-$NAME-$$")
  [ "$lock" = 1 ] && args+=(--lock)
  [ -n "$max" ] && args+=(--max "$max")
  REMOTE_UNIT="nxeon-dev-$NAME-$$"
  trap cleanup_remote_unit EXIT
  trap 'exit 130' INT TERM HUP
  local rc=0
  bh_ssh "$(q "$BH_TOOL/bin/run-capped.sh" "${args[@]}" -- "$@")" </dev/null || rc=$?
  REMOTE_UNIT=""
  return $rc
}

Deliberately separate from * lib/blog.ts's `renderMarkdown`, which stays first-party-only (blog posts, * admin docs, announcements, What's New) and keeps its simple * "escape everything, no raw HTML ever" model — that's correct for content * this repo's own authors write, but wrong here. * * WHY THIS EXISTS (2026-09-24 NxLabs description-gap fix): real Modrinth * project bodies routinely embed raw HTML inline with markdown — confirmed * live against the real API: `sodium`'s body contains literal `
`, * ``; BepInExPack_Valheim's Thunderstore README contains `
`, * `
`. Piping that through lib/blog.ts's `esc()`-first renderer turns * every tag into visible literal text ("<center>This mod...</center>") * instead of rendering it — exactly the bug this module fixes. * * SAFETY MODEL: every input is HTML-escaped FIRST (nothing here ever trusts * a raw `<` from an upstream source). A fixed ALLOW-LIST of simple tags is * then selectively restored by matching the ALREADY-ESCAPED text against * exact literal patterns (e.g. `<center>` -> `
`). An arbitrary * string from a mod body can never forge its way back into a real tag * unless it exactly matches one of the patterns below — attribute VALUES * (img src, a href) are extracted, validated (https-only, no javascript:/ * data:), and re-emitted through a fresh, controlled template; the * attribute text itself is never echoed back verbatim. This is why this * approach is safe against injection despite rendering third-party-authored * HTML, without pulling in a new npm dependency (this repo's own convention * — see lib/blog.ts's own hand-rolled renderer, components/ui/charts.tsx's * dependency-free SVG charts). * * HEADING POLICY: every in-body heading (markdown `#`/`##`/`###`, BBCode * [h1]/[h2]/[h3]) is capped at `

` — the page around this content already * has its own `

` (the mod name) and `

` ("Description"); a mod author * should never be able to inject a second, competing one. */ function esc(s: string): string { return s.replace(/&/g, "&").replace(//g, ">"); } function escAttr(s: string): string { return esc(s).replace(/"/g, """); } /** * Quote-only escape for a value that has ALREADY been through `esc()` once * (used inside `inlineMd`/`inlineBB`, both of which call `esc()` on their * whole input up front — see each function's own first line). Applying the * FULL `escAttr` (which re-runs `esc()`) there would double-encode: a real * `&` in e.g. a CDN image URL's query string (`?w=200&h=100`) is already * `&` by this point, and a second `esc()` pass would turn that into * `&`, corrupting the URL. Only `"` survives an `esc()` pass * untouched (esc() only ever touches `&`/``), so only `"` still needs * neutralizing here to keep a value safe inside a double-quoted attribute. */ function escAttrPostEscaped(s: string): string { return s.replace(/"/g, """); } const CLS = { h3: "mt-6 mb-2 text-lg font-semibold text-white", p: "mb-4 leading-relaxed text-slate-300", ul: "mb-4 list-disc space-y-1.5 pl-6 text-slate-300 marker:text-brand-400", ol: "mb-4 list-decimal space-y-1.5 pl-6 text-slate-300 marker:text-brand-400", li: "leading-relaxed", a: "text-brand-300 underline decoration-brand-300/40 underline-offset-2 hover:text-brand-200", img: "w-full rounded-xl border border-white/10 shadow-lg shadow-black/20 my-4", code: "rounded-md border border-white/10 bg-white/[0.06] px-1.5 py-0.5 font-mono text-[0.85em] text-brand-200", pre: "mb-4 overflow-x-auto rounded-xl border border-white/10 bg-navy-950/80 p-4 font-mono text-[13px] leading-relaxed text-slate-200", blockquote: "mb-4 border-l-2 border-white/15 pl-4 italic text-slate-400", hr: "my-6 border-white/[0.08]", }; /** * Only http(s) allowed, https FORCED (audit: "force https on embedded * images"). Protocol-relative `//host/img.png` gets an https: prefix. * Anything else (data:, javascript:, blob:, bare text) is rejected — the * caller drops the element entirely rather than render a broken/unsafe one. */ function safeImageSrc(u: string | null | undefined): string | null { 251:export function truncateMarkdown(md: string, maxChars = 6000): { text: string; truncated: boolean } { 262:export function renderModMarkdown(md: string): string { 355:export function renderBBCode(bbcode: string): string { 445:export type ModBodySource = "modrinth" | "thunderstore" | "steam_workshop" | "other"; 452:export function renderModBody(rawBody: string, source: ModBodySource, maxChars = 6000): { html: string; truncated: boolean } {

content.thinking:
I'm wondering if the portal's light theme remaps Tailwind color classes like text-white via generated CSS variable overrides, and whether the CyrusModView on the /mods/cyrus route inherits those portal light-theme tokens.

Now I'm sketching the data model additions to Prisma for a creator-customized mod listing, thinking through a CyrusModListing table tied one-to-one with CyrusModPage. The tricky part is that syncCyrusModPage currently overwrites the title from the project doc each time, so I need the listing to take precedence over synced data, or better, have title edits in NxLabs propagate back into the project's build metadata so both stay consistent.

I'm working through the remaining fields — tagline, description, icon/banner keys, tags, links, category, a per-version changelog, and a remix policy that defaults to open since most Cyrus mods ship under permissive licenses anyway.

I decide to keep this listing data in a new `CyrusModListing` table keyed by pageId rather than adding nullable columns to the existing model, since that avoids touching CyrusModPage and plays nicer with merges. I'm also sketching a separate `CyrusModMedia` table for gallery photos with id, pageId, userId, and key fields.

For media storage, I'm planning our own store under MODBUILD_DIR/nxlabs-media processed through sharp, served via an API route that checks page visibility before granting access. For remix tracking, I'm working through how CyrusFork resolves sourceBuildId to show which version of the original a fork is based on.

I realize that for fork-of-fork chains, sourceBuildId points to the original service build, losing the immediate parent's version—so I'm considering either adding nullable columns like parentBuildId and parentRootBuildId directly to CyrusFork, or creating a separate CyrusRemixLink table to track parent page, parent build, root origin, depth, and prompt history for the chain.

Given the rule to keep edits to shared schema files additive and appended at the end, modifying CyrusFork in place is riskier for merges, so I'll add a new CyrusRemix model at the end of the schema, keyed by the fork root build id, with legacy forks falling back to deriving their parent from existing CyrusFork data. I also need to figure out how the "Remixed from X by Y" credit chain gets preserved by walking through the mod page relationships.

For prompt history, I'm realizing that since readCyrusMeta only returns known keys and strips unknowns, I can't rely on CyrusMeta to carry prompt history forward -- I need to store that separately in a dedicated history field on CyrusRemix instead.

Actually, there's a simpler route: I could seed the project's notes field with a "Remixed from X by Y" header plus a formatted prompt history, since that's visible and editable in Cyrus's Notes tab, and change requests on the fork already use sourceBuildId as base so the service retains code context. I also need to make sure remixed code gets re-scanned through the existing safety scanner before any build runs, so I'm now locating that scanner in the modbuilder lib.

Let me check whether there's a portal-side scanner beyond the build service's own safety check. For "Community versions" on the original page, I'm thinking through showing all public, non-hidden forks (and maybe descendants) with their succeeded versions, author, base version, version notes, a diff view comparing remix source to base source, and a test status combining build success, safety verdict, and compile results.

For the diff view, I need source from both builds. I'm figuring out that the download route fetches source as a zip, so I'll build a dedicated diff endpoint that pulls both builds' source from the service, computes line-level diffs per file, and returns JSON for the client to render. The original author should also be able to pin or endorse one remix version to feature in the listing.

Now I'm designing a "Cyrus library" table linking users to pages with a unique constraint, so library mods show up as read-only branch nodes on the map. Selecting one opens a panel with Code, Versions, and Notes tabs plus "Remix" and "Install" actions — but installing raises a wrinkle since loadCyrusJar currently assumes the build chain's owner matches the server owner, so I need to work out how installing someone else's public library mod should actually function.

Since public pages already expose their jar via a public download route, I decide extending loadCyrusJar to permit installs when the page is public and not hidden introduces no new exposure, and I plan to pair that with ensureCyrusGameMod per root while tracing through how InstallModal's existing build-based install flow would plug into this.

This overlaps with the lifecycle agent's territory for server installs, so I want to keep my change minimal — just the one-line registry tweak plus a server action that routes through the same mods engine via enqueueModOp, after I check how installBuildToServer and the install route currently validate build ownership.

For creator profiles, I'm thinking through how to identify creators in the URL since users lack a handle field. I could expose the user cuid directly, but a cleaner approach is a `CyrusCreator` table with userId as id, a unique handle, and bio — lazily created when a creator first publishes or visits their profile, with the handle defaulting to a slugified display name plus a short id.

Simplifying further, I land on routing by handle (`/dashboard/nxlabs/cyrus/u/[handle]`) with lazy creation via a helper function. Then for collections, I need a `CyrusCollection` table (userId, unique slug, title, description, visibility) and a `CyrusCollectionItem` join table for pages within a collection, with routes on the creator profile and a dedicated collection page, plus core actions to create/add/remove/view.

Now I'm working out the community-tested status, defining a pure function that checks the page is public and not hidden, and requires a minimum number of distinct installing accounts other than the creator.

I need to pin down what counts as a real install -- distinct non-creator users with INSTALLED rows in ServerMod -- and realize there's no ratings system yet, so I'm sketching one: a `CyrusModRating` table limited to users who've actually installed the mod, making ratings more credible than open voting. The emerging criteria: at least 5 distinct non-creator installers, at least 3 ratings averaging 4.0+, and no open bug reports against the current version.

I'm also thinking the current version should target the latest supported Minecraft version, pass the safety check, and have been live for some minimum period like 3-7 days before it can earn laurel status, with a checklist UI showing creators which criteria are met. For version compatibility tags, I want to combine the declared build-against versions from doc.compat.mcVersions with actual observed server game versions pulled from INSTALLED ServerMod rows.

Beyond that, I'm planning per-version changelog notes that creators can override, a remix tree visualization built as a pure function rendering an indented tree with connectors, and extending the existing post-level report/moderation system to also cover pages or listings, possibly via a new report model.

Rather than reusing the post report flow directly, I'm leaning toward a generic reporting model keyed by target kind (page, collection, or media) with a unique constraint per user/target, reusing the same audit logging and admin review flow, and considering auto-hiding media after enough reports accumulate.

Prioritizing the build order: listing editor and photos first, then remix and community versions, then library, stars, compat tags, fork graph, profiles, collections, and reporting last — collections can stay lighter weight. For the UI, I need an "Open in NxLabs" button on the real mod preview panel linking to the project's editable page, but I need to figure out how to get the page slug into that view since it isn't currently carried through.

I'm thinking a server action like `openInNxLabs(rootId)` that ensures the page exists and returns the href is cleaner than a direct API call, since pages might not be synced yet. For library nodes, I need to add `libraryMods` state additively to the shared store, extend the Mod type with an optional library field, and have the preview panel render a dedicated library panel when that field is present.

Now I'm checking how the network graph draws mod pills by category to figure out how to add a subtle read-only marker for library mods, likely reusing scoreCategory from real.ts to classify them against the existing CATEGORIES set while constraining to the right game.

There's also a routing agent reworking universal categories, so I need to keep my category logic isolated to avoid merge conflicts. Then I'm planning the CyrusModView header: custom icon or seal fallback, optional banner background, title, tagline, and a credit chain showing remix lineage.

I'm also mapping out tabs — Overview with description, gallery, links, tags; Versions with changelog notes; new Community versions and Remix tree tabs (possibly merged); and a Community tab for threads. Then there's the owner edit mode, triggered via an edit flag or button, that opens a ListingEditor for managing title, tagline, icon/banner uploads, gallery, markdown description, tags, links, per-version changelogs, and visibility settings.

For the BuiltWithCyrusBadge, since that branch doesn't exist yet in the repo, I'll need to create it myself with props for variant (pill/laurel/shield), theme, size, and className, using the provided PNG brand assets in dark and light versions.

To avoid binary file conflicts if the studio-ui agent also copies these same assets, I'll place mine under `public/cyrus/community/` instead of the shared brand path, flagging the duplication for the merge coordinator to dedupe later.

/* ── one dial for icon size, site-wide ────────────────────────────────────
   Every mark in the system is drawn a fixed multiple of the size its call site
   asks for. Applying it HERE rather than editing hundreds of call sites keeps
   the relative sizing intact: an icon that was deliberately smaller than its
   neighbour stays proportionally smaller, it is just bigger in absolute terms.
   Change this one number to retune the whole set.

   Note for anyone adding a primitive: scale exactly ONCE per rendered mark.
   `Plate` draws an `Icon` inside itself, so it scales its own BOX and passes
   the raw size through — scaling in both places would compound to 2.25x. */
export const ICON_SCALE = 1.5;
export const iconPx = (n: number) => Math.round(n * ICON_SCALE);

/**
 * One interface mark.
 *
 * VECTOR FIRST, sprite as the fallback. `lib/nx/icon-paths.ts` carries the set
 * redrawn as 24x24 paths; anything it defines renders as an inline SVG in
 * `currentColor`, and anything it doesn't — the sheet's brand row (linux,
 * docker, postgres…) and the five 3D product renders — still comes off
 * `public/nx/nxicons.webp` exactly as before.
 *
 * Why the switch is here rather than at 137 call sites: the sprite's marks are
 * pre-coloured, so one inside a tinted control renders in the SHEET's colour
 * instead of the control's (a teal shieldcheck on a violet "Admin" chip is the
 * bug that started this). Routing both through one component means every call
 * site gets `currentColor` without being edited, and a name with no vector yet
 * silently keeps working.
 *
 * `size` still means what it always did — ICON_SCALE is applied here for BOTH
 * paths, so a swap is 1:1 and `Plate` (which sizes its box with `iconPx`)
 * needs no change.
 */
export function Icon({
  name, size = 20, className = "", style, strokeWidth = 1.8, tone,
}: {

content.content:
### B. Cyrus mods

A **Cyrus mod** is one `ModBuild` version chain (all versions share `rootBuildId`).

**B1 — engine installs + Installed list + badge.** Builder installs now go through the mods engine instead of the old direct copy:
- `lib/cyrus-mods/registry.ts ensureCyrusGameMod(root)` upserts a `GameMod` (`gameFamily=minecraft`, `source="cyrus"`, `sourceId=rootBuildId`, `slug=cyrus-<root>`, **`active=false`** so it never appears in the catalogue / store / NxLabs listings / sitemap; also excluded from cross-provider dedupe).
- `lib/mods/installers/cyrus.ts` is the "cyrus" source of the Minecraft installer: it reads the jar from the jar store (sha256 checked against `ModBuild.jarSha256`), only for Paper/Purpur, and only for the server owner's own builds (`loadCyrusJar`), and hands it to the engine as a prefetched `plugin-jar` package keyed `cyrus:<root>` (versionId = build id). Nothing is downloaded.
- `lib/modbuilder/install.ts installBuildToServer` queues `INSTALLING`/`UPDATING` with **`ServerMod.targetVersionId` = the build** (new nullable column) through `enqueueModOp` (per-server lock), then waits up to 45 s for the worker so the Cyrus install modal can still say "done" (`queued: true` when it didn't finish in time). The route response is unchanged plus `queued`/`modId`. The worker (`worker/game-mods.ts`) passes `targetVersionId` into `CatalogFacts`, records `ServerMod.versionId` for Cyrus rows, and clears the target.
- Engine state, backups, rollback-on-failure, enable/disable (Paper plugins are SAFE), uninstall: all the stock engine (`lib/mods/engine.ts`), now returning `versionId` in `OpOk`.
- **Pre-engine installs**: a jar an older builder install copied (not in `state.json`) is shown under Installed as "copied here before the Mods tab tracked them" with **Manage here** (`trackCyrusInstall`), which backs it up to `/root/.nxeon-mods/backups/<stamp>-cyrus-adopt-<name>/` and reinstalls the same build through the engine. The first engine install on a server the old path touched does the same adoption automatically.
- Badge: `components/nx/CyrusBadge.tsx` (`CyrusBadge`, `CyrusSeal`) — a ringed-monogram seal + small caps, token colours, `tone="onDark"` for dark islands. **Every** Cyrus surface renders the mark only through this file, so the Cyrus redesign can swap it in one place.
- Servers listed in the Cyrus install modal now need to be RUNNING (the engine installs onto the running server); stopped ones show "start it to install".

**B2 — updates, history, rollback.** `getModsOverview` adds `cyrus` to each Cyrus row (`lib/cyrus-mods/installed.ts`: installed vs current version, labels like `v2 · 1.1.0`, update available, version count, page slug) and sets `availableVersion` from the chain (so the update badge and the Updates count include it). The **Versions** dialog (`mods/CyrusVersions.tsx`, actions in `lib/actions-cyrus-installed.ts`) lists every finished version newest first with its release notes (the builder's own "what changed", else the change request), marks "On this server" / "Latest", offers **Update to latest** and **Roll back to this** (confirm step; one engine `update` job with `targetVersionId`; the replaced jar is backed up). "Latest" = the creator's restored head in Cyrus (`cyrus.headBuildId`) when set, else the newest success. Two versions with the same version string get a distinct package version (`1.1.0+<id6>`), so the engine's idempotency check can't skip a real switch.

**B3 — auto-generated pages.** `lib/cyrus-mods/doc.ts buildModDoc(chain)` (pure) → `CyrusModPage.doc`: name (Cyrus title, else plugin name), tagline, summary, how to use, limitations, commands, permissions, config, compatibility (Paper/Purpur + every MC version built for), versions + changelog, current version, source file list. `lib/cyrus-mods/pages.ts syncCyrusModPage(root)` creates the page when a chain's **first** version succeeds and regenerates it on every later one (hooked into `lib/modbuilder/store.ts syncBuild`, so both the API routes and the worker sweep trigger it; never fails a build). Older builds are backfilled when their creator opens the Cyrus Mods page. Slugs: kebab of the name, de-duplicated.
- Routes: portal `/dashboard/nxlabs/cyrus` (index: your mods + published ones, search) and `/dashboard/nxlabs/cyrus/<slug>`; public `/mods/cyrus` and `/mods/cyrus/<slug>` (`app/(marketing)/mods/cyrus/**`; the middleware keeps them out of the NXM rewrite and its anonymous cache header). NxLabs home gets a **Cyrus Mods** section and tab (`LabsTabs cyrus`) for gated viewers.
- Page: header (seal, title, badge, creator display name — never any part of an email — version, licence, forks, "forked from"), Overview / Versions / Community tabs, download source + jar per version, sha256, Build on this.
- **Open source**: every page offers the source. `/api/nxlabs/cyrus/<slug>/download?what=source|jar&build=<id>` (gated like the page, rate-limited 30/10 min) serves the jar from the store and the source zip from the build service — cached on the primary as `<jar dir>/<id>.source.zip` after the first fetch — repacked with `LICENSE` and `NXEON-CYRUS.md`. Licence: **MIT by default**, creator-selectable from MIT / Apache-2.0 / MPL-2.0 / GPL-3.0-only / BSD-3-Clause / Unlicense (`CYRUS_LICENSES`). MIT and Unlicense texts are reproduced in full; the others ship a copyright line + SPDX id + the canonical SPDX URL (owner decision whether to embed full texts).
- **Private by default.** Only the creator can publish (`setCyrusPageVisibility`, with a confirm that says exactly what publishing means) or make it private again. Admins can hide a whole page.

**B4 — community.** `CyrusModPost` threads (`parentId=null`) and comments, `kind` NOTE / BUG / FIX, `status` OPEN / RESOLVED, optional `buildId` (a version of this mod; a bug report must name one when there are several). Rules in `lib/cyrus-mods/community.ts` (pure, tested): resolve = thread author, creator, admin; delete = author (own), creator, admin (thread delete takes its replies + reports); hide/unhide = creator, admin; report = any signed-in viewer except the author, once per post (`CyrusModReport`), **auto-hidden at 3 reports** until reviewed. Rate limits are DB counts (hold across processes): 5 threads/hour, 30 comments/hour, 20 reports/day per user, 10 forks/hour. Posting needs a verified email. Every write is refused while an admin is impersonating (writes need the real signed-in account to be the effective one; reads show what the customer sees). Every action is audited (`cyrusmods.*`).
- **Build on this mod** (`forkCyrusMod`): the creator just opens their version in Cyrus. Anyone else (who has Cyrus access) gets their OWN copy of the chosen published version: a new succeeded `ModBuild` (jar copied, docs copied, title "<name> (fork)") + `CyrusFork{buildId, sourceBuildId, sourcePageId}`; their copy gets its own private page with "forked from". Change requests on the copy are sent to the build service with the ORIGINAL build as base (`serviceBuildId()` in `app/api/mod-builder/builds` POST, `/source`, `/source-zip`), because the service only knows the original. Forks of forks resolve to the original.
- Admin: `/admin/cyrus-mods` (URL-only; ADMIN + preview allowlist): launch switch, open reports (Hide / Dismiss), all pages.

**Gating (must stay hidden until launch).** `lib/cyrus-mods/gate.ts`: allowed = Setting **`cyrus_mods_public_enabled`** (default `"false"`) OR a modbuilder preview account (`preview_access_emails_modbuilder` / `preview_access_emails`, default the owner). Outside the gate every route 404s (titles say "Page not found"), every action answers "Not found", downloads 404, the NxLabs section/tab are not rendered, pages are `noindex`, and nothing is in the sitemap. After launch: published pages are visible to everyone (indexable), private pages still only to their creator/admins; the sitemap lists `/mods/cyrus` + published pages (`lib/sitemap-sections.ts`). Building on a mod still requires Cyrus access (private preview). **To launch:** `/admin/cyrus-mods` → "Launch Cyrus mods publicly" (or set the Setting). Not done: a "Cyrus Mods" link on the PUBLIC NxLabs page `/mods` — that page is generated (`tools/nxm/port_pages.py`), so add it through the generator at launch.

**Schema (additive, `prisma db push`):** `ServerMod.targetVersionId String?`; new tables `CyrusModPage`, `CyrusModPost`, `CyrusModReport`, `CyrusFork` (FK-less ids). No existing column changes.

**Mod health.** Cyrus rows record `ServerMod.fileName` (the jar the engine placed), and `lib/mod-health.ts nameForms` now also tries the jar name without its version suffix (`Heal-1.1.0.jar` → `Heal`), so a Cyrus mod whose page title differs from its plugin name still gets a verdict.

**Known limits.** Cyrus mods are skipped by the auto-updater (no upstream; they change only when the owner picks a version). Installing someone else's published Cyrus mod straight onto your server is not offered (download the jar, or Build on it to get your own copy) — owner decision.

**Verified in a sandbox harness (2026-10-07, throwaway DB `nxeon_agt_cyrusmods`, local mock of the build service serving REAL build records/jars/sources fetched from it earlier, the REAL `gameModSync` handler on a fake guest dir):** builds synced through `syncBuild` generated their pages; Cyrus install → engine → `state.json` + `ServerMod.versionId`; Versions dialog Update to latest (v1→v2, old jar backed up), Roll back (v2→v1), switch off/on (staged → one batch job), "Manage here" adoption of a pre-engine jar; publish; another preview account posted a bug on v1, the creator replied with a FIX and resolved it, the other account reported the reply (report row + count) and forked the mod (own private page "forked from"); source zip download (LICENSE + NXEON-CYRUS.md inside) and jar download; `/admin/cyrus-mods` launch switch on → outsider/anonymous get the published page (indexable) but still 404 on private pages, sitemap lists `/mods/cyrus` + the published page only; switch off → 404 + noindex again, nothing in the sitemap. NOT verified on a real game server (no customer servers touched; no throwaway VM provisioned).

Tests: `test/cyrus-mods.test.ts` (doc generation, slugs, licences, package versions, gate decisions + a source check that every route/action/download is gated, community rules, and the REAL engine path for a Cyrus jar against a fake guest: install → idempotent → update → disable → enable → rollback → refuse foreign version → uninstall, plus non-Paper and checksum refusals). Verification notes + screenshots: `/root/agent-notes/cyrus-mods/`.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

# Cyrus v6 community: notes for the merge + owner

Branch `feature/cyrus-v6-community` (worktree /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-community). Full write-up:
docs/DOCUMENTATION.md "Cyrus community (v6)".

## Migration
Additive only. `npx prisma db push` creates 10 new tables (CyrusModListing, CyrusModMedia, CyrusRemix,
CyrusModStar, CyrusModRating, CyrusLibraryItem, CyrusCreator, CyrusCollection, CyrusCollectionItem,
CyrusCommunityReport). No existing table/column changes, no relations, no data-loss prompt expected.
Images are stored under MODBUILD_DIR/nxlabs-media (same disk as the jars).

## Merge points (shared files, all small + additive)
- lib/cyrus/types.ts: `Mod.library?`
- lib/cyrus/store.ts: `libraryMods` + `setLibraryMods`; useAllMods/findMod/useMod include them
- lib/cyrus/forge.ts: refuse prompting a library node ("Remix it first")
- components/cyrus/cosmos/graph.ts + Network.tsx + app/dashboard/cyrus/studio.css: `is-library` pill
- components/cyrus/preview/PreviewPanel.tsx: library branch + NxLabs button in the mod header
- components/cyrus/CyrusApp.tsx: `<CyrusLibrarySync />`
- lib/cyrus-mods/registry.ts loadCyrusJar: others' servers may take PUBLISHED mods (mayInstallChain)
- lib/actions-cyrus-mods.ts forkCyrusMod -> delegates to remixCyrusMod (no unscanned fork path left)
- prisma/schema.prisma: block at the end
- Duplicates to reconcile: `components/cyrus-mods/BuiltWithCyrusBadge.tsx` + public/cyrus/community/badge-*.webp
  (studio-ui owns components/cyrus/brand/); `ModListingInput` in lib/cyrus-mods/listing.ts (routing owns
  lib/cyrus/listing.ts: re-export this superset); categories come from lib/cyrus/data CATEGORIES today,
  swap to routing's universal list (saveModListing + edit page + library.ts).
- lifecycle agent: `switchCyrusVersion` (lib/actions-cyrus-installed.ts) still checks `b.userId !== server.userId`;
  for community installs it should use `mayInstallChain` too, otherwise switching versions of an installed
  community mod says "Not found".

## Owner decisions
1. Default remix setting = OPEN (code is open source anyway). OK?
2. Installing someone else's PUBLISHED Cyrus mod on your own server is now offered (was "not offered").
3. Community-tested thresholds: 5 other accounts, 3 ratings avg >= 4.0, no open bugs on current version,
   newest MC, safety pass, 7 days out. Tune?
4. Ratings only from installers (anti-spam). Stars from anyone signed in.
EOF

input.message:
**Community (Cyrus v6): all the code is written and committed. It has not been checked in a browser.** Per your wrap-up message I stopped before seeding and screenshots and wrote PAUSED.md.

Branch `feature/cyrus-v6-community`, commit `93d9da2d18`, worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-v6-community`.

**Checks**
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean on node-2.
- `test/cyrus-community.test.ts` showed no failures. It checks listing validation, remix permissions, the credit chain, the remix tree, Community-tested criteria, rating rules, compatibility tags, the re-scan, `mayInstallChain`, and that every new action, route and page is behind the gate.
- `test/cyrus-mods.test.ts` fails at import: `lib/auth` → `lib/geo-ip` → `server-only`. I didn't change anything in that import chain and believe the failure was already on the base branch, but I didn't run it there to confirm.
- The schema pushes cleanly to the node-2 throwaway DB.
- Not run: the seed, the dev server and the screenshots. The seed hit the 10-minute command limit on a loaded node-2 before printing anything.

**What was built**
1. **Open in NxLabs**: an NxLabs button in Cyrus's mod panel, and an "Edit listing" page at `/dashboard/nxlabs/cyrus/<slug>/edit`. The creator can set title (it also renames the Cyrus project), short description, category, tags, icon, banner, a photo gallery of up to 12, a markdown description (the existing sanitiser, images stripped), links, per-version changelog notes, visibility and the remix setting.
   - Saving goes through `saveModListing(projectIdOrBuildId, input)`. It also accepts the routing agent's `ModListingInput` shape.
   - Images are re-encoded to WebP and served with the page's own visibility rule.
2. **Remix in my Cyrus**: honours the creator's remix setting (OPEN by default).
   - Before anything is copied, the jar's checksum is checked and the build service's source safety rules are re-run (ported to TypeScript). If the builder is offline the remix is refused.
   - The copy opens in Cyrus with "Remixed from…" and the original's prompt history in its Notes, and a `CyrusRemix` row records its lineage.
   - The old `forkCyrusMod` now goes through the same path, so there is no unscanned fork route left.
3. **Credit and Community versions**: the header shows "Remixed from X by Y · originally Z by W". A new "Community versions" tab lists published remixes at any depth, each with the version it was built on, its notes, test status, a source diff against that base, and a pin button for the original creator. A remix tree sits below it.
4. **Add to my Cyrus**: community mods show on the map as read-only dotted pills. Their panel has code, versions and about, plus "Install on my server", "Remix" and "Remove". Prompting on one of these mods says "Remix it first".
5. **Community features**:
   - Stars, and 1–5 ratings that only accounts which installed the mod can give.
   - A **Community-tested** status worked out from real data on every page load, never set by hand. It needs: published; on 5+ other accounts' servers; 3+ ratings averaging 4.0+; no open bug on the current version; built for the newest Minecraft version; passed the safety check; out for 7+ days. Earned → the laurel badge; otherwise the page shows the checklist.
   - Compatibility tags state only facts ("Built for MC x", "Running on N servers", "Needs an update").
   - Creator profiles (`/u/<handle>`), collections (`/c/<slug>`, with a "Save to collection" menu), reports on pages, photos, collections and profiles, and an admin queue for them.
6. **Schema**: 10 new tables at the end of `schema.prisma`; existing tables are untouched. A plain `prisma db push` should create them with no data-loss prompt.
